record.context_brief: Harmonious labelings of even torus grids
record.original_question: For positive integers m and n, in all cases not already covered by m = 1 and n > 1, does the Cartesian-product torus grid C_{4m} x C_{2n} admit a harmonious labeling? Here C_r is the cycle with r vertices, C_{4m} x C_{2n} is a Cartesian-product grid on a torus, and a harmonious labeling of a connected graph with e edges assigns distinct vertex labels from 0 through e - 1 so that edge sums are distinct modulo e.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C_r$ denote the cycle graph on $r$ vertices, and let $G \square H$ denote the Cartesian product of graphs $G$ and $H$. A harmonious labeling of a connected graph $G$ with $e$ edges is an injection $f$ from the vertex set of $G$ into $\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$ such that, as $uv$ ranges over the edges of $G$, the edge sums $f(u)+f(v) \pmod{e}$ are all distinct (and thus take every value in $\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$).

For positive integers $m$ and $n$, consider the torus grid graph $C_{4m} \square C_{2n}$. Excluding the trivial degenerate case $m=1$ with $n>1$ already settled, determine whether $C_{4m} \square C_{2n}$ admits a harmonious labeling for every remaining pair $(m,n)$ of positive integers.
artifact.status_search_result: Gallian's Dynamic Survey of Graph Labeling lists the harmonious labeling problem for Cartesian products of cycles $C_m \times C_n$ as largely unresolved; the parity necessary condition fails for many residue classes, but the case $C_{4m} \times C_{2n}$ (with $4m\equiv 0\pmod 4$ and $2n$ even) is not ruled out and no general construction or proof appears in the literature. No source found establishes a complete solution, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: A Dynamic Survey of Graph Labeling (Gallian)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of harmonious labelings of Cartesian products of cycles, noting necessary parity conditions and unresolved cases.
status_evidence.claim: The harmonious labeling status of $C_{4m}\times C_{2n}$ is not established in general in the standard survey.

status_evidence.title: Harmonious Graph -- Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: Standard definition of harmonious labeling for graphs with e edges.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the harmonious labeling definition used in the problem.
